doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Wish list and Rickie Lee Jones
summary: Artists Pallo would like to play with, such as Eric Clapton and k.d. lang, and working with Rickie Lee Jones.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Neat. Who were some of the — is there anybody that you haven’t worked with that you’d like to?
Yeah. Yes, yes. There’s quite a few. One, as far as a musician or entertainer.

It doesn’t matter who, either way. Well Clapton, Eric Clapton I never had an opportunity to do anything with him, meaning like either a session or have him sit in. He would be one. And gee there are some singers I would love to, but I can’t think of them right now, but there’s a few, like Diana Krall is very — k.d. lang.

Isn’t she? They would be something, because I love backing up people. That’s always been my thing is to play behind them and try to make them sound as best as I can do for them. Rickie Lee Jones I played for a few times. You’ve heard of her?

Excellent, excellent singer, excellent. I couldn’t believe — I mean she is, and she would do standards but with Rickie you can’t play too much. She’ll say, “Give me a chord,” you give her a chord, she sings maybe a measure and a half and then you can give her another chord. But don’t try to play anything in between. She wants to do it with her voice. She was tough to work for but she was a great entertainer, a great singer too.
Yeah. Did she do more sort of rubato, out of time singing?
That’s tough like when to — you want it now?
A lot of rubato. And a lot of Sinatra stuff. She did a lot of his songs. And I worked with her three times. She was great to work with. So many.
